userStories.title: [E17] Production regular expressions linear, not timed
userStories.description: Found in ARV-156 and rated by its security review: 12 production `[GeneratedRegex]` rules backtrack under a match timeout (Site.CodePattern, TopologyCodes.Code, FlightRules.Carrier and Codeshare, OutboundRules.PathAndQuery and Scope, EmailAddresses.Rule, EmailTemplates.Placeholder, CsvImportReader.Number, the Cronz JobsDashboardGuard rules), and three interpreted calls also check the clock (Email.cs:199, JobsDashboard.cs:30 and :32). A timeout is wall-clock time, so a loaded node can raise RegexMatchTimeoutException on a short input: it fails closed (DependencyOutage treats it as no outage, the handler answers 500 without detail, a check never passes), so this is robustness rather than security, but it can give a rare 500 or a failed start under load. CWEs to review: CWE-1333, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: Every anchored production rule above runs on RegexOptions.NonBacktracking without a timeout (captures and unanchored search work on it); the linear engine is the ReDoS bound, stated in the CWE-1333 row

TopologyCodes.Code drops its lookahead for a length check (1 to 16) plus `^[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*\z` on NonBacktracking, proven equivalent by a CsCheck property comparing old and new rules on random strings of up to 20 characters over A-Z, 0-9, '-', '\n', lowercase and non-ASCII; parity with script 0008's CHECK and varchar(16) kept

The RedactionEnricher rules keep no timeout (a timeout in a Serilog enricher would throw and could let an event out unredacted); the FloorPlanFiles backreference rule stays anchored and bounded; both are named in the CWE-1333 row with their reason
A test per rule asserts its options and infinite timeout, and each rule's accepted set is unchanged (existing tests plus a table per rule)

userStories.title: [E6] Dead letters: text PostgreSQL accepts and a per-topic relay hold
userStories.description: From the ARV-171 security review (PASS, 2026-10-13), three non-blocking findings. (1) A NUL character or a lone surrogate in a record's key, a header name or value, or the error message makes the keep fail (PostgreSQL text refuses 0x00 in message_key, and CAST AS jsonb refuses \u0000 and unpaired surrogates in the payload), so such a record still ends on ARV-166's unacknowledged path; it needs a buggy or hostile Kafka producer, which is what the unreadable path is for. (2) A dead-letter row that fails with a broker error ends the relay pass like any broker failure; a .dlq.v1 topic that hangs (its leader away while domain topics are fine) holds each attempt up to the 45 s produce bound and can delay domain events by up to 45 s repeatedly during the short backoffs. (3) The app charts set no terminationGracePeriodSeconds (Kubernetes default 30 s) and no host sets HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (.NET default 30 s), while one in-flight message can need the rest of its retry schedule (at most 3 x 5 s), the keep (at most 10 s) and the consumer close. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: DeadLetters.Create replaces NUL and lone surrogates with U+FFFD in the key, header names and values and the error message, and flags the letter when it did (a header naming what was replaced, never the original bytes); OutboxKeyOf uses the digest when the key held such a character; the letter's topic, partition, offset and consumer stay exact so a replay can still fetch the original record

A .dlq.v1 row whose send fails with a broker error holds back only its topic for the rest of the relay pass instead of ending the pass, so domain rows keep draining; a domain row's failure still ends the pass as today

Unit tests: a letter with "\0" in a header and in the key is kept and its row key is the digest; a lone surrogate in the error message is replaced; a failing .dlq.v1 row leaves a domain row of the same pass sent. Integration test: a record whose key and headers carry a NUL is kept at a stop and its row read back
The residual text that names this case (ConsumeFilters, overview Producing, ADR-0018 in a new dated note, wiki 10 section 4.5a) says it is closed

userStories.title: [E18] Web requests bound to the account that started them
userStories.description: Follow-up from the ARV-104c security review (2026-10-09, Low). Api.ts recovers a 401 by refreshing the session and sending the request again. A request started by one account that is still in flight when that account signs out and another signs in on the same browser is then sent again under the second account, or its recovery signs the second account out; an MFA step-up can be shown to the second account for the first account's action. ARV-104c closed this for the capture calls only (asSubject). The server still applies the second account's permissions and site scope and audits it, so the exposure is small, but a request must never change hands. Epic: Accounts and sessions. CWEs to review: CWE-384, CWE-863, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: Api.ts request() records auth.subject when a call starts and uses it as the default for asSubject: once a different account or none is signed in, the request is not sent, not sent again after a refresh, and does not trigger the 401 recovery (no refresh, no sessionEnded, no MFA step-up)
Callers that legitimately run before a subject exists (sign-in, refresh, MFA enrolment) keep working, named explicitly in code

Playwright: a save on an administration screen held in flight across a sign-out and another account's sign-in in the same page is never sent under the second account, the second account stays signed in and sees no step-up prompt; existing session, MFA and multi-tab tests still pass

userStories.title: [E6] A host's own disposal never dead-letters a valid message, and the broker probe names no topic
userStories.description: From the ARV-165 security review (PASS, 2026-10-14), two low findings. (F2) The stop budget covers the retry schedule and the 10 s keep but not the consumer's own time per attempt: when attempts are slow at a stop (a database stall at Npgsql's 30 s command timeout), MassTransit's stop wait can end with a message still in its retries; the host disposes its container while the bus keeps stopping in the background, the later attempts fail with ObjectDisposedException, and the final attempt keeps the dead letter, so a valid event lands in the dead-letter topic (a replay is needed), or is faulted when the database is away too. Wiki 10 section 4.5a states the case and the replay meanwhile. (Probe) KafkaProduce.BrokersAnswerAsync calls GetMetadata(timeout), which asks for every topic on the cluster; on a large or shared cluster the reply is large. A metadata request that names one topic is not the answer: Confluent.Kafka 2.15.1 documents allow.auto.create.topics as true by default for producer-type clients (the admin client is one), so naming a missing topic can create it with the broker's defaults, AMAN's topics included (seen in ARV-176's first baseline). CWEs to review: CWE-400, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: A failure caused by the host's own disposal while its endpoint stops (ObjectDisposedException from the host's services, or an equivalent signal) does not dead-letter the message: the record is left unacknowledged so it is delivered again after the restart, without opening the ARV-166 skip (prove the checkpointer cannot pass it)

The readiness probe names no topic: it uses IAdminClient.DescribeClusterAsync on the producer's handle within the same 3 s bound, single-flight and reused for 1 s, and still reports Degraded within its bound when no broker answers. A metadata request naming one topic is not used (it lets a broker with auto.create.topics.enable create the topic with broker defaults). If DescribeCluster proves unsuitable, keep GetMetadata(timeout) for all topics, whose cost is bounded at one request a second per pod

Ariva's producer and admin client configurations set AllowAutoCreateTopics = false (KafkaClientConfig), with a test proving that a send or a metadata read for a missing topic does not create it, so no Ariva client can create a topic implicitly whatever the cluster's setting; the relay and Ingest treat the resulting unknown-topic failure as the row's own failure
Unit tests for both; an integration test where a slow attempt outlasts the bus's stop wait and the message comes back after the restart instead of reaching the dead-letter topic
Wiki 10 section 4.5a no longer describes the edge case as open

userStories.title: [E4] Sensing resends: late receipt-timed resends and bounded declarative names
userStories.description: Two low findings from ARV-174 (2026-10-14). (1) The engineer's: a receipt-timed message resent more than about three minutes after the first (the queue engine's RecentBatches window) is applied again live while the archive keeps it once (its id window is three days), so live and replayed counts differ; no shipped mapping stamps crossings at receipt, so the pilot is not affected. (2) The ARV-174 security review's recommendation 1: a declarative mapping that reads a name or id from the group (^) or payload ($) level makes DeclarativeMapper.State.Name and Id call GetString() per item, a fresh copy each time (2,000 items x up to about 500 KB, roughly 1 GB), and the batch id's encoding would copy and sort it again; latent, since no shipped mapping does this. CWEs to review: CWE-400, CWE-120, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: A receipt-timed resend later than the engine's window is either recognised live (a longer window for receipt-timed kinds, bounded in memory) or stated as a residual with the live and replay difference documented in formulas F5 and sensor-adapters.md, with a test either way

The declarative mapper caps name and id lengths at the canonical maxima, refusing longer values as a format error, or refuses ^ and $ rooted name and id paths when a mapping is parsed; a test with a mapping that would have copied a large group-level string per item

userStories.title: [E17] Monitoring metrics: bounded feed tags, the outbox count off the relay's path, and the gaps the pilot can live with
userStories.description: Low findings from ARV-125a (2026-10-14). From its security review: (1) ariva.flights.items, ariva.feeds.went_stale and ariva.feeds.recovered are tagged with the feed name an authenticated integration client chooses (any normalized 2 to 32 character name per known site), so now that the meter is exported the OpenTelemetry SDK's default of 2,000 points per metric stream is the only per-pod bound; (2) OutboxRelay awaits MeasureIfDueAsync before each pass, so in a large backlog (after an outage, when draining matters) a slow count(*) can hold a pass up to 10 s every 30 s. From the engineer: (3) the ARV-125b AMAN feed alert, based on the records counter, cannot tell sites apart; a per-site feed age gauge from the desk feed's heartbeat would; (4) lag of the MassTransit consumer groups can only come from the broker or the site's collector; (5) while the stream worker's reading is paused (a zone at its bound with the database away) the fetched watermark does not move, so ariva.stream.consumer_lag stays flat instead of growing (the database alert covers that case). CWEs to review: CWE-400, CWE-532.
acceptanceCriteria: Feed tags are bounded: an unknown feed is reduced to `other` (only feeds the site has configured keep their name), or the feed is bound to the client; MetricTagTests' allowlist commentary says so, with a test that a new client-chosen feed name does not add a series

The outbox measurement runs on its own timer, never before a relay pass, or its count is capped (for example at 100,000, reported as at least), with a test that a slow measurement does not delay a pass

A per-site AMAN feed age gauge exists (from the desk feed's heartbeat, no desk or officer data), or the residual is stated in wiki 10 section 2a; the MassTransit consumer lag and the flat stream lag while reading is paused are stated there as known gaps with the alert that covers each
